title: How heavy are the five heaps of rice?
description: Five heaps of rice, each ten times heavier than the one before, are added in grams and changed to kilograms. One milligram is then written in grams. Keeko's doubt is that one milligram is zero point zero one grams.
teaching_notes: One idea: write every heap in the same unit before adding, then change the total. Watch for students who add numbers from different units.

source: Rice heaps start at 1 g and each next heap is 10 times heavier. Show the five heaps weigh 11.111 kg together, then write 1 mg in grams.
video_script.why: The child has changed grams into kilograms and now adds weights of different sizes first.
video_script.substitution: Write every heap in grams, add them, then change the total to kilograms.
video_script.anchor: five heaps of rice, each ten times heavier than the one before
video_script.wrong_move: takes a milligram as a hundredth of a gram
video_script.payoff_line: Add in grams, then change the total to kilograms

final_answer.spoken: eleven point one one one kilograms; one milligram is zero point zero zero one grams

maths_rules: 11111 g = 11.111 kg, since 1000 g make 1 kg
the slip: 0.01 g would be 1/100 g, but a gram has 1000 mg
video_script.design: The five heaps stay in the anchor band, each ten times the one before. They slide into the working band as grams and are added; the total is changed to kilograms. A last step splits a gram into milligrams.
open_questions: The rice heap picture could not be read from the book text; the five heaps 1 g, 10 g, 100 g, 1 kg and 10 kg come from the worklist.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book, then five heaps of rice: 1 g, 10 g, 100 g, 1 kg and 10 kg; a question mark in the anchor band

marks.list: the five heaps are drawn in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about five heaps of rice.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The first heap is one gram, and each next heap is ten times heavier.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must show that all five weigh eleven point one one one kilograms. Then we write one milligram in grams.

beats.on_screen: the heaps stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 1 kg = 1000 g and 1 g = 1000 mg shown as two small scales; each heap is 10 times the one before

marks.ten: an arrow shows each heap multiplied by ten

narration: <bookmark mark='scales'/>A kilogram has one thousand grams, and a gram has one thousand milligrams.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Each heap is ten times the one before, so we multiply by ten again and again.

beats.on_screen: Given: heaps of 1 g, 10 g, 100 g, 1 kg and 10 kg
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, heaps of one gram, ten grams, one hundred grams, one kilogram and ten kilograms.

beats.on_screen: To find: the total weight in kg, and 1 mg in g
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the total weight in kilograms, and then write one milligram in grams.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: in grams the heaps are 1, 10, 100, 1000 and 10000

marks.same: every heap is written in grams
marks.list: the five numbers are listed in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step one, write every heap in the same unit, grams.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The heaps are one, ten, one hundred, one thousand and ten thousand grams.

marks.add: the five numbers are added in a column

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step two, add the heaps. They have a one in every place, from ones up to ten thousands.
<bookmark mark='total'/>The total is eleven thousand one hundred eleven grams.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 11111 g = 11.111 kg, since 1000 g make 1 kg

marks.kg: the point moves three places left

narration: <bookmark mark='kg'/>Step three, one thousand grams make a kilogram, so the point moves three places left.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Eleven thousand one hundred eleven grams is eleven point one one one kilograms.

marks.thou: 1 mg is written as one thousandth of a gram

narration: <bookmark mark='mg'/>Step four, one gram is one thousand milligrams.
<bookmark mark='thou'/>One milligram is then one thousandth of a gram.
<bookmark mark='dec'/>That is zero point zero zero one grams.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Add in grams, then change the total to kilograms.
<bookmark mark='kg'/>The five heaps weigh eleven point one one one kilograms in all.
<bookmark mark='mg'/>One milligram is zero point zero zero one grams.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the heaps
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 1 mg = 0.01 g appears and is struck out; a gram scale shows 1000 milligram marks; 0.001 g is written

marks.fix: 0.01 is struck out and the 1000 marks are shown

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one milligram is zero point zero one grams, because a gram has one hundred milligrams.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a gram has one thousand milligrams, not one hundred.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>One milligram is one thousandth of a gram, which is zero point zero zero one grams.
